A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StreamingThinker. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–F support a reliable comparison, with no material reading gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original Qwen3 experiments across mathematical reasoning, logical reasoning and context-based QA, including accuracy, token usage, latency and efficiency measurements in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons, attention analyses and the efficiency evaluation.

M1.justification: The streaming CoT generation pipeline, attention mask, position encoding, controllable reasoning depths and parallel KV-cache inference are unchanged (Sections 2–3; Appendices C and E).

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same six evaluation benchmarks across math, logic and context-based QA, the TuLu-personas-math-grade training source, and question-first and context-first scenarios (Section 4; Appendix D).

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–4 is unchanged. The added 'without distillation' wording in Tables 1–2 restates the original batch baseline's lack of additional supervision already described in v2 Section 4.1.

E3.justification: Dataset splits and filtering, Qwen3 model sizes, training settings, reasoning depths, evaluation metrics, the 150-word-per-minute input rate and the 100-sample efficiency study remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The reasoning-depth and position-encoding analyses, attention maps, input-order comparisons and efficiency analysis retain the same evidence. Appendix examples, prompting observations and sentence-similarity analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Repeated-run, seed and uncertainty reporting is unchanged. Both versions present the same point-estimate reporting without confidence intervals or significance tests for the experimental comparisons.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4, Figures 4–5 and the appendix examples and similarity maps retain the same numerical values and qualitative findings. No result entries are added, removed or corrected.

T1.justification: The formal streaming definition, attention-mask and position equations, quality-score definitions in Appendix C.4 and latency definition in Appendix F.2 are unchanged. No theoretical results or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same novelty and contribution claims, including comparable reasoning performance, an 80% reduction in token waiting and over 60% lower answer latency.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning input order, conservative local reasoning, deferred global integration and cache efficiency remain unchanged. Appendix A.2 retains the controlled-testbed scope and proposed future extension to complex streaming scenarios.

D1.justification: The abstract changes 'Code will be released' to 'Code is publicly available' while retaining the same repository link. This updates reported resource availability; implementation and training disclosures otherwise match. Repository contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds Zhao et al. (2026), On-policy supervised fine-tuning for efficient reasoning, under token compression, and Lin et al. (2026), Speak while watching, under streaming modality adaptation. The broader research positioning and earlier cited works are retained.

P1.justification: Limited wording edits clarify baseline captions and code availability. Author affiliations are revised and an ICLR 2026 publication header is added; the narrative, section order and appendix prose otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 receive revised captions, and conference running headers are added. There is small local reflow of text, figures and references, while figure designs, table structures and appendix displays are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 makes Tables 1–2 easier to interpret independently by explicitly identifying the undistilled original baseline, and updates the abstract from a promised code release to reported public availability. These provide limited gains in clarity and reproducibility information, alongside two added related-work citations. The scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged.
